newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Securum sells three properties in London, Munich.
newsitem.headline: Securum sells three properties in London, Munich.

text.p: Sweden's state-owned holding company Securum AB said on Friday it freed up more than 1.7 billion crowns selling two properties in London, and one in Munich.
Securum said in a release that it had sold a building in west London to German property company Despa for about 530 million crowns.
It had also sold a central London office building to the German property fund Difa for about 340 million crowns.
Additionally, the company divested the Sheraton hotel in Munich to Germany's Schorghuber group for an undisclosed sum.
"Through these three sales Securum has freed up over 1.7 billion crowns," Securum said.
Securum is a state-owned company set up to manage assets pledged by Swedish banking group Nordbanken during the bank crisis in the early 1990s.
It aim is to divest all assets at a reasonable price.
